questions.question: Why must a good leader listen to people? Give an example.
questions.expected_answer: A leader must listen so that they know what people really need and can make decisions that help them; listening also makes people feel respected. For example, Mama Nomsa asked families what they needed before starting the soup kitchen, and Desmond Tutu listened to thousands of people's stories at the Truth and Reconciliation Commission.

questions.question: What does it mean to be a servant of the people?
questions.expected_answer: It means the leader believes their job is to serve the people and puts the people's needs first, instead of using their position for money, special treatment or power.

questions.question: Give one example of a leader who worked for the good of others, and explain what they did.
questions.expected_answer: Albertina Sisulu worked for many years as a nurse and midwife in Soweto and opened her home to people in need, while fighting against apartheid. Or Desmond Tutu spoke out against apartheid and later for the poor and people with HIV.
